content:
eli: EDR flagged a suspicious DLL dropped into /tmp on maria-dev01 and injected into code-server process. quarantine kicked in automatically.
sec_ops_bot: Device isolated from network (isolation_id: iso-1964812300). File quarantined: /tmp/.svc-helper.so. SHA256 logged.
maria: Whoa. I was testing a local build of a native helper for a service. I used a prebuilt binary from home, could that be it? I didn't run anything weird.
chris: Collected artifact and hash: SHA256=3b9f4d1e5a2c9f0e8a1b7b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2. VirusTotal shows no hits. Path executed by pid 3421 -> /usr/bin/code-server.
jamie: Can you confirm the parent process tree? Need to know if it spawned from a terminal or via remote session.
chris: Parent tree: /usr/bin/systemd -> /usr/lib/code-server/bin/code-server -> pid 3421. No sshd parent.
nate: @maria do you have any mounted network shares or dev containers that could've supplied that .so? Also rotate any keys if you touched private repos?
maria: I was mounting a docker volume from my macbook and copying a .so I compiled locally. I did use scp earlier today to copy the build artifact. No private repo changes.
eli: Since quarantine already happened, let's run local triage commands and an EDR deep scan. @maria please run:
```
sudo /opt/edr/bin/edrctl collect --type=process --pid=3421 --out=/tmp/triage-1964812300.tar.gz
sudo /opt/edr/bin/edrctl scan --full
```
chris: Also upload /tmp/triage-1964812300.tar.gz to the secure bucket and post the link here. I'll look at network indicators and process memory.
maria: Uploading now to s3://redwood-sec-triage/maria/1964812300.tar.gz (presigned link posted).
sec_ops_bot: Scheduled host re-scan in 1 hour and enabled elevated logging for code-server.
jamie: If this is a benign dev build, let's add a temporary allowlist for that hash while we confirm to avoid repeat quarantines. But only after chris confirms no IOCs.
chris: Memory dump shows no network beacons. No persistence traces in systemd units or cron. The .so does export an oddly named symbol (svc_init) but looks like a dev helper.
eli: Good. Still treat like untrusted until we confirm chain-of-custody for the artifact. @maria, who did you scp from? IP or host?
maria: scp from my macbook-loc IP 10.0.0.15 over our VPN. The macbook scanned clean last night.
nate: Let's rotate any tokens that were on that laptop as a precaution. I'll open a task to rotate CI deploy tokens and any user PATs for maria.
chris: Marking this as "investigation - likely benign" for now. Will keep quarantined artifact until end of day. If no new indicators, we'll release hold and add a one-off allowlist entry for developer artifacts from that user.
eli: Post-incident actions: 1) Require devs to sign native builds or use attested artifacts for remote copying. 2) Add doc in devex about safe copying for mac<->linux builds. 3) Add automated EDR rule that checks code-server module loads for untrusted /tmp libraries.
maria: Agree on the docs. Sorry for the noise — I should've used the build pipeline instead of scp.
jamie: Thanks all. If anything changes, mention @eng-security and reopen. :thumbsup:
